message.reasoning_content:
The kernel prunes the ReLU residual. Key question: is the residual always ≤1.0 error over the box? With adversarial inputs (max dot products), residual = 0.25*sum relu(...). b = 0.75*|W|row sum, so max possible dot(W,x) = sum|W|. Max relu = 0.25*sum|W|. Residual sum could be up to 0.25 * sum over 6 neurons of 0.25*|W|j = 0.25*0.25*sum|W|. Actually relu(dot - b) max = sum|W| - 0.75 sum|W| = 0.25 sum|W|. Each |W| row sum: 12 entries of 0.5 or 1.0 → 6..12, so 0.25*rowsum ≤ 3. Total residual ≤ 0.25*sum_j 0.25*rowsum_j. If all magnitudes 1.0, sum_j rowsum = 72, residual max = 0.25*18 = 4.5 > 1. But actual magnitudes vary. Need to compute actual W. Also note relu(dot - b) requires all entries aligned with W signs — achievable within [-1,1] box. So max residual = 0.25 * sum_j (0.25*|Wj|sum) = 0.0625*sum|W|. If sum|W| > 16, error > 1. Need to check actual parameters. Also there's random x constraint? No, x can be any box point. So probe: compute W, construct x = sign(W) rows, check error.

But wait: max error = residual only if residual positive; error = |target - base| = residual. So compute worst-case. Run probe.
